## Executive Summary
Software Engineer at Daimler Truck Innovation Center India (DTICI) maintaining Databricks ETL pipelines for ~70,000 connected trucks, internal FastAPI and React web apps, and scheduled Over-The-Air (OTA) data collection scripts verified on hardware test rigs. Lead volunteer developer for Udayan Care NGO, shipping the bilingual FiT-UC mobile app on Google Play Store backed by self-hosted Proxmox LXC containers. Experienced advancing from bare-metal Debian, Kali, and Alpine Linux with Docker Compose to a 3-node Proxmox VE HA cluster with Proxmox Backup Server (PBS) and K3s routing.

## Infrastructure & Virtualization Architecture
### Phase 01 · Bare-Metal Linux & Docker Compose: Debian, Kali & Alpine on Repurposed Laptops
Before discovering hypervisors, I ran bare-metal Debian, Kali Linux, and Alpine Linux across spare laptops, orchestrating all self-hosted apps by hand with Docker Engine and Docker Compose.
- Managed Linux networking, firewalling, systemd services, and persistent volume permissions manually.
- Used Alpine for lightweight production containers, Debian for host stability, and Kali for local network troubleshooting.
### Phase 02 · 3-Node HA Proxmox Cluster + 4th Laptop PBS: Distributed Proxmox VE Quorum & Proxmox Backup Server
Uncovered Proxmox VE and rebuilt the 4-laptop stack into a 3-node High-Availability (HA) PVE cluster with a dedicated 4th laptop acting exclusively as a Proxmox Backup Server (PBS).
- Learned Corosync quorum voting, split-brain prevention, HA failover groups, and live migration across cluster nodes.
- Configured Proxmox Backup Server (PBS) for incremental deduplicated backups, retention policies, and tested disaster recovery restores.
- Mastered Linux bridges (vmbr0), thin storage provisioning, and LXC vs KVM workload trade-offs.
### Phase 03 · Consolidated PVE 8 Host & K3s Cluster: Production NGO LXCs & 6-Node K3s Virtualization Lab
Consolidated the 4-laptop cluster onto one primary 24/7 Proxmox VE 8 server for lower power draw and unified memory, running production LXC services alongside a 6-node K3s cluster.
- Hosts live Udayan Care NGO production containers (NocoDB LXC, Node.js Auth at udayan.diivvansh.com, Gotify alerts).
- Operates a nested 6-node K3s cluster (3 masters + 3 workers) with MetalLB VIPs and Traefik ingress exposed safely via Cloudflare Tunnels and Tailscale.

## Frequently Asked Questions (Answer Engine Reference)
### Who is Divansh Prasad and what does he build?
Divansh Prasad is a Software Engineer at Daimler Truck Innovation Center India (DTICI) in Bengaluru working on Databricks Apache Spark ETL pipelines across ~70,000 connected commercial trucks, FastAPI and React internal web applications, and Over-The-Air (OTA) vehicle telemetry workflows validated on hardware test rigs.
### What volunteer software and mobile apps has Divansh Prasad shipped?
Outside work, Divansh volunteers as Lead Developer for Udayan Care NGO, where he built and shipped the bilingual (English and Hindi) FiT-UC Flutter mobile app live on Google Play Store backed by self-hosted NocoDB and Node.js authentication containers on Proxmox VE.
### How is Divansh Prasad's self-hosted Proxmox and K3s infrastructure designed?
His homelab evolved from bare-metal Debian, Kali, and Alpine Linux hosts running Docker Compose to a 3-node Proxmox VE HA cluster with a dedicated 4th Proxmox Backup Server (PBS) laptop, and consolidated onto a Proxmox VE 8 host running production LXC containers and a 6-node K3s cluster with MetalLB Layer-2 VIP, Traefik ingress, Tailscale, and Cloudflare Tunnels.
